title: Braves call-up prospect Owen Murphy to boost injury-depleted pitching staff
content:
ATLANTA — With injuries taking a toll on their pitching staff, the Atlanta Braves are calling up right-hander Owen Murphy. Murphy, the Braves’ No. 11 prospect, according to Keith Law, is expected to join the team Monday. He is slated to pitch out of the bullpen.

The 22-year-old had a 3.88 ERA with 65 strikeouts and 20 walks in 60 1/3 innings at Triple-A Gwinnett after starting five games in Double-A Columbus to begin the season.

The Braves selected Murphy with the No. 20 pick of the 2022 MLB Draft out of Riverside-Brooks High School (Illinois). Murphy had Tommy John surgery in 2024, but returned in 2025 and has continued to pitch well.

He has a three-pitch mix with a fastball that sits at 91-92 mph, which is slower than most but plays well because of its flat-angle approach. He also has a mid-80s slider and mid-70s curveball.

Murphy takes the place of Martín Pérez on the active roster. Pérez was placed on the injured list with a left forearm contusion after getting hit by a comebacker from Juan Soto in Sunday’s 10-9 loss. 

In addition, JR Ritchie, who pitched three scoreless innings and recorded the save in Saturday’s 14-3 win, was recalled, while Carlos Carrasco was designated for assignment for the sixth time this season.
